start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-what-a-list-says-true with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_me on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-me-postgres-connection\"}, list_id docs and action {\"action\": \"set_up\"}."
no_lists_because: The list is the one you name by list_id, kept in your own store; this item names no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-what-a-list-says-true" with store, the list_id and the action: set_up first, then verify, flag_outdated, request_verification or assign on the rows you name.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts: the prove step must give every expected outcome and row value, or the run stops and says which.
4. To see what needs review, ask your AI for the rows needing review: tool:find-rows-needing-review reads the list's saved views over the rows you hand it.

worked_examples.title: Set a docs list up for review and verify a row
worked_examples.ask: Set up my docs list for review, then mark the onboarding row as checked by me.
worked_examples.given: The docs list is kept in the store with its title and body fields, and the look step found it not yet set up for review.
worked_examples.hands_back: results [{set_up true, fields_added [owner, review_state, review_due, verified_by], views_added [review-needed, review-expired, review-empty], expires_days 90}, {action verify, kept [row-1]}], kept_records [the docs definition, row-1], and row-1 read back as Verified with a check-again date 90 days ahead.
